# BepInExPack Valheim: Recent Version Changelog

## Version 5.4.2351
Logging improvements include plugin GUIDs in startup messages and chainloader completion counts. Fixed Valheim version display and duplicate GUID warnings. Doorstop updated to stock UnityDoorstop 4.5.0, supporting older Linux systems with glibc 2.7+.

## Version 5.4.2350
Updated to "BepInEx 5.4.23.5 from 5.4.23.3." Fixed semver version strings like "1.1.0-beta.2" that were previously rejected. UnityLogListener consolidated for Unity 6 compatibility. Chainloader now handles stripped Unity log callbacks and macOS fixes.

## Version 5.4.2333
"Unity 6 compatibility: We now bind directly to Unity's real UnityEngine.UnityLogWriter." Resolves startup failures on Valheim 0.221.3 with Unity 6000.0.46f1. Added safety probing for method hooking and fallback to legacy stub for older versions.

## Version 5.4.2332
Corrected filename to "libdoorstop_x64.so" (previously misnamed).

## Version 5.4.2331
Updated "libdoorstop_x64.so to target glibc 2.34 by compiling against Ubuntu 22.04." Restores compatibility with Ubuntu 22.04 and Debian 12. Systems using Debian 11 or older are no longer supported.

## Version 5.4.2330
Removed "Valheim.DisplayBepInExInfo.dll" from default package. Updated BepInEx from 5.4.22 to 5.4.23.3 and Doorstop to v4.4.0. Replaced startup script with community-tested version.

## Version 5.4.2202
Preloader patching adjusted. Unstripped Corlibs remain removed. Preloader version incremented.

## Version 5.4.2201
"As of Valheim 0.217.24, there is no longer a need for unstripped corlibs." Removed corlibs and updated Doorstop configuration accordingly.

# Jotunn Changelog: Versions 2.20-2.30

## Version 2.30.3
Fixed custom categories not displaying ghost items when first equipped after game start.

## Version 2.30.2
Addressed Deep North assets overriding vanilla mocks and legacy build menu compatibility issues.

## Version 2.30.1
- Introduced `PieceConfig.Usage` for build menu tag customization
- Added `PieceTableConfig.GuessUsage` option
- Deprecated piece table category API
- Fixed TerrainOp registration to ObjectDB systems

## Version 2.30.0
Updated for Valheim 1.0.7; piece categories require overhaul as the system was completely restructured by the game.

## Version 2.29.2
Corrected `InputManager.AddButton` registration timing for buttons added after ZInput initialization.

## Version 2.29.1
Fixed ZoneLocation syncing, SoftReference spawning, minimap texture mismatches, and network version lookups.

## Version 2.29.0
- New ConsoleCommand method accepting Terminal context parameter
- TMPro FontAssets shortcuts added to GUIManager

## Version 2.28.0
- YAML localization support
- macOS development support
- Fixed skill name persistence after language changes

## Version 2.27.1
- Vulkan compile target fix for internal AssetBundles
- SoftReference asset release handling correction

## Version 2.27.0
- `AssetUtils.LoadImage` wrapper for .netstandard compatibility
- `AssetUtils.DuplicateTexture` for readable texture copies

## Version 2.26.1
Corrected GUI initialization for Valheim 0.221.3 with backward compatibility.

## Version 2.26.0
- **CustomLocation loading via SoftReferenceableAssets** reduces memory by loading only when needed
- `AssetManager.ResolveMocksOnLoad` option
- `AssetManager.OnSoftReferenceableAssetsReady` event

## Version 2.25.0
- Unresolved mocks now log warnings without blocking CustomEntity addition
- Mock warning aggregation (up to 5 issues per object)
- Fixed dedicated server mock resolution
- Custom categories now supported beyond ID 100
- Fixed admin list watcher redundancy

## Version 2.24.3
- `ConfigFileWatcher` for filesystem-based config reloading
- RequirementConfig overloads simplification
- Changed Local AdminOnly initialization timing to ZNet.Start

## Version 2.24.2
Fixed black screen on server crossplay connections and error handling for servers without mods.

## Version 2.24.1
Fixed GUI compatibility for Valheim 0.220.3.

## Version 2.24.0
- `ConfigFileWatcher` class introduction for dynamic config reloading
- ConfigFile BindConfig extensions for convenience

## Version 2.23.2
Corrected CustomGUIFront/CustomGUIBack offset positioning.

## Version 2.23.1
Fixed RPC routing to prevent duplicate sends or incorrect targeting.

## Version 2.23.0
Added ConfigFile BindConfig/BindConfigInOrder extensions; fixed ConfigurationManager compatibility.

## Version 2.22.0
- `SynchronizationMode` attribute for AdminOnly config handling customization
- **Mod detection now uses GUID instead of name**
- Conflict resolution with `__state` patches during ModQuery operations

## Version 2.21.3
Fixed category tabs refreshing every frame, causing sapling spinning in cultivator.

## Version 2.21.2
Updated for Valheim 0.219.14 (Bog Witch); older versions unsupported.

## Version 2.21.1
Corrected config value changes in main menu error handling.

## Version 2.21.0
- **DungeonManager with CustomRoom and RoomConfig** for custom dungeons
- **PieceManager.AddPieceCategory(string name)** overload; deprecated table-based variant
- Exact version matching requirement for server/client Jotunn compatibility

## Version 2.20.3
Fixed explicit `AdminOnly = false` config locking and improved performance for large config file searching.

## Version 2.20.2
- Admin-only config locking refinement between menu and game load
- Network version constant access correction
- GUIManager prefab cache usage and crash prevention

## Version 2.20.1
Fixed item cloning with ExtEquipment; changed ItemManager.Items to dictionary structure.

## Version 2.20.0
Compatible with Valheim 0.218.15 (Ashlands); added HeavyBuild to PieceCategories; fixed category positioning.

# Valheim 1.0 Technical Details for Server Owners

## Version & Release
- **Release Date:** September 9, 2026
- **Current Build:** 1.0.14 (as of September 17, 2026)
- **Hotfixes:** 1.0.10/1.0.12 (September 11), 1.0.14 (September 17)

## Save Format Changes
The world structure was redesigned: instead of `.fwl` and `.db` file pairs, worlds now exist as folders containing `".fwl2, .db2 and .chunks files plus a"` cache directory. Existing worlds convert automatically on first 1.0 server load.

## Engine & Modding
The engine upgraded to a newer Unity version, which broke most mods at launch. Mod authors received no public test branch before release.

**BepInEx Requirements:**
- Update the BepInEx loader before updating plugins
- Update shared libraries (Jötunn) before individual mods
- Enable one mod per restart to identify errors
- Mods without updates since September 9 should remain disabled

## Server Configuration
No new or changed launch arguments. Existing flags work unchanged: `-crossplay`, `-name`, `-world`, `-password`, `-port`, and world-modifier flags.

## Player Cap & Crossplay
- Player cap remains 10 (described as "a game for 1-10 players")
- Crossplay now includes PS5 and Switch 2 (previously Xbox only)
- Console players cannot install mods; server-only mods remain compatible
- Join code system unchanged: six-digit codes for console access

## Version Matching
Clients and servers must match versions. A 1.0 client cannot join an early-access server.

## Hotfix Highlights
**1.0.12:** Banlist/whitelist accept both old `Steam_` and new `V_` ID formats; fixed item stand durability loss; added achievements opt-in command.

**1.0.14:** Fixed terrain modifications causing performance/portal issues in multiplayer.

# ServerSync Overview

## Purpose
ServerSync is a library for synchronizing configuration between game servers and clients, enabling version control and configuration management for BepInEx mods in Valheim.

## Key Usage

**Initialization:**
Developers create a ConfigSync instance with a unique identifier: `"new ServerSync.ConfigSync("my.mod.guid") { DisplayName = "My Mod Name", CurrentVersion = "1.2.3"..."`

**Core Methods:**
- `AddConfigEntry<T>()` registers BepInEx config entries for synchronization
- `AddLockingConfigEntry<T>()` registers entries that control whether configs are locked based on their values

**Version Control:**
CurrentVersion triggers warnings if server/client versions mismatch. MinimumRequiredVersion enforces compatibility—clients with older versions disconnect with an explanatory error message.

**Custom Data:**
The `CustomSyncedValue<T>` class synchronizes arbitrary data beyond standard config entries, with Value properties and change event handlers.

## Distribution & Integration

ServerSync is embedded into mods via **ILRepack**, a NuGet package. The ILRepack.targets configuration file merges ServerSync.dll into the mod's primary assembly, ensuring the dependency is bundled invisibly.

## License

ServerSync uses the **MIT-0 license**, granting users essentially unrestricted use without attribution requirements.

# Thunderstore Package Format Requirements

## Required Files

A valid package must be a ZIP containing three files at the root:

1. **icon.png** – "PNG icon for the mod, must be 256x256 resolution"
2. **README.md** – Markdown file rendered on the package page
3. **manifest.json** – JSON metadata file
4. **CHANGELOG.md** (optional) – Change history

## manifest.json Fields

| Field | Rules |
|-------|-------|
| `name` | "no spaces. Allowed characters: a-z A-Z 0-9 _" Max 128 characters |
| `version_number` | "following the semantic version format Major.Minor.Patch" |
| `description` | "Max 250 characters" |
| `dependencies` | Array of dependency strings in format `{team}-{package}-{version}` |
| `website_url` | Optional URL; use empty string if omitted |

## README.md Validation

- Markdown syntax with GitHub-compatible formatting
- "has to be UTF-8 compatible"

## ZIP Layout Requirements

Files must reside "at the root of the zip." Zipping a directory instead creates an invalid package structure where files are nested in a subdirectory rather than at root level.

## Size Limit

Maximum package size is approximately 5 GB, though this is adjustable upon request.

content.content:
# NxeonDevAdmin

A small BepInEx plugin for Valheim. It lets a player who is on a dedicated
server's `adminlist.txt` use cheat console commands (`god`, `fly`,
`debugmode`, `ghost`, `spawn`, `nocost`, `exploremap` ...) while connected to
that server.

**It has to be installed on the PLAYER'S PC** (their BepInEx /
r2modman / Thunderstore profile). A copy on the server alone does nothing for
players. Version 1.0.0 (2026-09-09 to 2026-10-01) was only ever installed on
servers, so it never unlocked anything for a connected player. The full
decompiled evidence is in `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md`, section "Valheim dev
commands: how it really works (2026-10-01)".

## How Valheim decides (build l-1.0.16, network version 40)

Decompiled from `assembly_valheim.dll` (sha256 `50035055f9b158a0...1e44e39fd`,
identical in the Steam dedicated-server depot and on a customer server):

```csharp
public bool IsCheatsEnabled() {           // Terminal
    if (m_cheat) { if ((bool)ZNet.instance) return ZNet.instance.IsServer(); return false; }
    return false;
}
public bool IsValid(Terminal context, bool skipAllowedCheck = false) {   // Terminal.ConsoleCommand
    if ((!IsCheat || context.IsCheatsEnabled()) && (context.isAllowedCommand(this) || skipAllowedCheck)
        && (!IsNetwork || (bool)ZNet.instance)) {
        if (OnlyServer) { if ((bool)ZNet.instance) return ZNet.instance.IsServer(); return false; }
        return true;
    }
    return false;
}
// Terminal.TryRunCommand: IsValid -> run locally;
//   else if RemoteCommand && client -> ZNet.RemoteCommand(text) (sent to the server);
//   else "'<cmd>' is not valid in the current context."
```

- The console (F5) runs every command **in the process where it was typed**,
  and checks it against that process's own state. For a player that is the
  game client, where `ZNet.IsServer()` is false.
- `devcommands` (not a cheat) toggles the client's own `Terminal.m_cheat` and,
  on a client, also sends `devcommands` to the server
  (`ZNet.RemoteCommand` -> RPC `RPC_RemoteCommand`). The server checks
  `adminlist.txt`, logs `Remote admin '<id>' executed command 'devcommands'
  remotely.` and runs it in the **server's** console, which toggles the
  **server's** `m_cheat`. Typing it 3 times toggles it on, off, on.
- `god`, `ghost`, `heal` are `isCheat: true`. `fly`, `debugmode`, `nocost`,
  `exploremap`, `spawn` are also `OnlyServer`. None of them is
  `remoteCommand: true`, so they are never sent to the server. On a client
  they fail `IsValid` and print `'god' is not valid in the current context.`
  That is the "unknown" Jay saw.
- Only commands built with `remoteCommand: true` (`sleep`, `skiptime`,
  `setkey`, `removekey`, `resetkeys`, `listkeys`, `players`, `genloc`,
  `setworldpreset`, `setworldmodifier`, `confirmcheats` ...) are forwarded.
  The server runs them if the sender is on adminlist, using the server's own
  `m_cheat` for the cheat ones. Vanilla already does this, with no mod.

So a server-side patch on `IsCheatsEnabled` cannot affect `god`/`fly`/
`debugmode`: they are never evaluated on the server. On the server itself the
1.0.0 patch could never change a result either: `IsServer()` is true there, so
vanilla already returns `m_cheat`.

## What 2.0.0 does (client side)

Only when the local player is a **client** (not the server or a listen host)
and appears in the admin list the server sends to every client on connect
(RPC `AdminList` -> `ZNet.GetAdminList()`):

1. `Terminal.IsCheatsEnabled()` postfix: also true when `m_cheat` is set.
2. `Terminal.ConsoleCommand.IsValid()` postfix: an `OnlyServer` command that is
   **not** `RemoteCommand` may run locally (`fly`, `debugmode`, `nocost`,
   `spawn`, `exploremap`, ...). Remote commands keep the vanilla forwarding.
   `Chat.isAllowedCommand` is still consulted, so cheats typed in chat stay
   refused.
3. `Game.isModded = true`. Iron Gate asks every mod to set this. It also
   means `Achievements.IsCheatedAtAll()` is true, so cheat commands skip the
   "type confirmcheats" prompt.

The admin check accepts the forms the server accepts: `Steam_7656...` and the
bare `7656...`. This matters: vanilla's client-side `LocalPlayerIsAdminOrHost()`
only matches the prefixed form (`PlatformUserID.ToString()` =
`"Steam_" + id`), and adminlist files written from the lloesche image's
`ADMINLIST_IDS` hold bare IDs. The server's own check (`ZNet.ListContainsId`)
accepts both.

The same DLL stays bind-mounted on BepInEx servers (`worker/game-config.ts`
`applyValheim`). There it changes nothing. Keeping it there is harmless and
keeps one artifact for both sides.

Not a security boundary: Valheim trusts the client for player state. Any
player who installs a cheat mod can already fly. This plugin just makes the
console behave for the server's listed admins.

## Customer instructions (r2modman / Thunderstore Mod Manager)

1. Get `NxeonDevAdmin.dll` 2.0.0 from Nxeon support. Do not use the server's
   current copy at `/opt/valheim/nxeon-mods/` until the 2.0.0 deploy has
   reached that server.
2. In r2modman, select Valheim and the profile you play with. Settings ->
   "Browse profile folder".
3. Open `BepInEx\plugins`, create a folder `NxeonDevAdmin`, put the DLL in it.
4. Start the game with "Start modded". In `BepInEx\LogOutput.log` look for
   `Nxeon Dev Admin 2.0.0 loaded`.
5. Join the server. Press F5. Type `devcommands` **once** (it should answer
   `Dev commands: True`). Then `god`, `fly`, `debugmode`.

Manual BepInEx install (no mod manager): same DLL into
`<Steam>\steamapps\common\Valheim\BepInEx\plugins\NxeonDevAdmin\`.

If F5 does nothing, the console is switched off. Turn it on in the game's
settings ("Enable console"), or add `-console` to Steam -> Valheim ->
Properties -> Launch options. Both exist in this build (`PlatformPrefs`
"EnableConsole" and the `-console` argument).

Other players do not need this plugin to join. It is not a gameplay mod. It
does not change world or network data.

## Rebuilding and testing

The game and BepInEx DLLs are never committed. `../NxeonDevAdmin.Harness/run.sh`
does everything without touching a customer server:

- installs the dotnet SDK under `/tank/tools/dotnet`
- downloads the public Valheim dedicated-server DLLs (Steam app 896660,
  anonymous, via DepotDownloader) and BepInExPack_Valheim from Thunderstore
- builds this plugin
- runs the dispatch harness

The harness loads the real `assembly_valheim.dll`, registers the real vanilla
commands (`Terminal.InitTerminal`), and drives the real
`Terminal.TryRunCommand` as a remote client. Only Unity-native calls are
stubbed. It runs vanilla, with this plugin, and with the committed DLL, for
bare, prefixed and missing admin entries.

Build only:

```bash
dotnet build -c Release -p:RefsDir=/path/with/0Harmony.dll,BepInEx.dll,UnityEngine*.dll,assembly_valheim.dll,assembly_utils.dll,Splatform.dll
# Output: bin/Release/net472/NxeonDevAdmin.dll -> copy over worker/assets/valheim/NxeonDevAdmin.dll
```

`test/valheim-devadmin-dll.test.ts` (part of `npm test`) statically checks
that the committed DLL matches the source version and has both patch targets.

After every Valheim update, run `run.sh` again before assuming the patch
targets still match.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build NxeonDevAdmin against the REAL game DLLs and run the dispatch harness.
#
#   tools/valheim-plugins/NxeonDevAdmin.Harness/run.sh [WORKDIR]
#
# Everything goes under WORKDIR (default /tank/tools/valheim-devadmin-work), never into the repo:
#   - dotnet SDK 8 + runtime 9    -> /tank/tools/dotnet       (dotnet-install.sh, no system install)
#   - Valheim dedicated server DLLs (Steam app 896660, anonymous, public) via DepotDownloader
#   - BepInExPack_Valheim (Thunderstore) for 0Harmony.dll + BepInEx.dll
# It never contacts a customer server. Needs internet the first time.
set -euo pipefail
HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
PLUGIN_SRC="$HERE/../NxeonDevAdmin"
WORK="${1:-/tank/tools/valheim-devadmin-work}"
DOTNET_DIR="${DOTNET_DIR:-/tank/tools/dotnet}"
export DOTNET_ROOT="$DOTNET_DIR" DOTNET_CLI_HOME="$WORK/dotnethome" DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT=1 NUGET_PACKAGES="$WORK/nuget"
DOTNET="$DOTNET_DIR/dotnet"
mkdir -p "$WORK"

if [ ! -x "$DOTNET" ] || ! "$DOTNET" --list-sdks | grep -q '^8\.'; then
  curl -sSL https://dot.net/v1/dotnet-install.sh -o "$WORK/dotnet-install.sh"
  bash "$WORK/dotnet-install.sh" --channel 8.0 --install-dir "$DOTNET_DIR"
fi
if ! "$DOTNET" --list-runtimes | grep -q 'NETCore.App 9\.'; then
  bash "$WORK/dotnet-install.sh" --channel 9.0 --runtime dotnet --install-dir "$DOTNET_DIR" 2>/dev/null \
    || { curl -sSL https://dot.net/v1/dotnet-install.sh -o "$WORK/dotnet-install.sh"; bash "$WORK/dotnet-install.sh" --channel 9.0 --runtime dotnet --install-dir "$DOTNET_DIR"; }
fi

MANAGED="$WORK/valheim-server/valheim_server_Data/Managed"
if [ ! -f "$MANAGED/assembly_valheim.dll" ]; then
  mkdir -p "$WORK/depotdl"
  url=$(curl -s https://api.github.com/repos/SteamRE/DepotDownloader/releases/latest \
    | python3 -c 'import sys,json;print([a["browser_download_url"] for a in json.load(sys.stdin)["assets"] if a["name"].endswith("framework.zip")][0])')
  curl -sSL -o "$WORK/depotdl/dd.zip" "$url"
  python3 -c "import zipfile,sys;zipfile.ZipFile(sys.argv[1]).extractall(sys.argv[2])" "$WORK/depotdl/dd.zip" "$WORK/depotdl"
  printf 'regex:valheim_server_Data/Managed/.*\\.dll\n' > "$WORK/depotdl/files.txt"
  "$DOTNET" "$WORK/depotdl/DepotDownloader.dll" -app 896660 -os linux -filelist "$WORK/depotdl/files.txt" -dir "$WORK/valheim-server"
fi
BEPCORE="$WORK/bepinex/BepInExPack_Valheim/BepInEx/core"
if [ ! -f "$BEPCORE/BepInEx.dll" ]; then
  mkdir -p "$WORK/bepinex"
  v=$(curl -s https://thunderstore.io/api/experimental/package/denikson/BepInExPack_Valheim/ | python3 -c 'import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)["latest"]["version_number"])')
  curl -sSL -o "$WORK/bepinex/pack.zip" "https://thunderstore.io/package/download/denikson/BepInExPack_Valheim/$v/"
  python3 -c "import zipfile,sys;zipfile.ZipFile(sys.argv[1]).extractall(sys.argv[2])" "$WORK/bepinex/pack.zip" "$WORK/bepinex"
fi

REFS="$WORK/refs"; mkdir -p "$REFS"
cp "$BEPCORE/0Harmony.dll" "$BEPCORE/BepInEx.dll" "$REFS/"
for f in UnityEngine.dll UnityEngine.CoreModule.dll assembly_valheim.dll assembly_utils.dll Splatform.dll; do cp "$MANAGED/$f" "$REFS/"; done
echo "assembly_valheim.dll sha256: $(sha256sum "$MANAGED/assembly_valheim.dll" | cut -d' ' -f1)"

# Build the plugin from a copy so bin/ and obj/ never land in the repo.
rm -rf "$WORK/plugin-build"; mkdir -p "$WORK/plugin-build"
cp "$PLUGIN_SRC/Plugin.cs" "$PLUGIN_SRC/NxeonDevAdmin.csproj" "$WORK/plugin-build/"
"$DOTNET" build "$WORK/plugin-build" -c Release -p:RefsDir="$REFS" -p:RestorePackagesPath="$NUGET_PACKAGES" -nologo -v q
PLUGIN_DLL="$WORK/plugin-build/bin/Release/net472/NxeonDevAdmin.dll"
echo "built: $PLUGIN_DLL"

rm -rf "$WORK/harness-build"; mkdir -p "$WORK/harness-build"
cp "$HERE/Program.cs" "$HERE/Harness.csproj" "$WORK/harness-build/"
"$DOTNET" build "$WORK/harness-build" -c Release -p:RefsDir="$REFS" -nologo -v q
OUT="$WORK/harness-build/bin/Release/net8.0"
for f in "$MANAGED"/*.dll; do b=$(basename "$f"); case $b in System*|mscorlib.dll|netstandard.dll|Mono.Security.dll) continue;; esac; [ -e "$OUT/$b" ] || cp "$f" "$OUT/"; done

rc=0
echo; echo "### vanilla client (must refuse god/fly/debugmode exactly like Jay saw)"
(cd "$OUT" && ADMIN_FORM=bare "$DOTNET" Harness.dll) || rc=1
for form in bare prefixed none; do
  echo; echo "### client + NxeonDevAdmin (source build), adminlist=$form"
  (cd "$OUT" && ADMIN_FORM=$form "$DOTNET" Harness.dll --with-plugin "$PLUGIN_DLL") || rc=1
done
COMMITTED="$HERE/../../../worker/assets/valheim/NxeonDevAdmin.dll"
echo; echo "### client + committed worker/assets/valheim/NxeonDevAdmin.dll, adminlist=bare"
(cd "$OUT" && ADMIN_FORM=bare "$DOTNET" Harness.dll --with-plugin "$COMMITTED") || rc=1
echo; [ $rc -eq 0 ] && echo "HARNESS: ALL RUNS PASSED" || echo "HARNESS: FAILURES (see above)"
exit $rc

/**
 * Valheim — BepInEx plugins from Thunderstore.
 *
 * Server: lloesche/valheim-server (prisma/catalog.ts), `-v /opt/valheim/config:/config`.
 * With the BepInEx server type (`BEPINEX=true`, worker/game-config.ts) the image
 * itself copies /config/bepinex/plugins into its BepInEx install on every
 * start — that folder is the documented drop point, and the only one this
 * installer writes to. BepInEx loads plugin DLLs recursively, so each package
 * gets its own `<Namespace>-<Name>` folder (the r2modman/Thunderstore
 * convention), which is also what makes uninstall exact.
 *
 * Package layout (Thunderstore's documented structure): manifest.json,
 * icon.png, README.md at the root, and the payload either at the root, under
 * `plugins/`, or under `BepInEx/plugins/`. Everything that isn't plugin
 * payload is handled explicitly:
 *   - `config/` defaults are skipped (BepInEx writes a config on first run);
 *   - `patchers/`, `core/`, `monomod/` need BepInEx's preloader folders, which
 *     this server type doesn't sync from /config — such packages are refused
 *     with that reason rather than installed half-working;
 *   - BepInExPack (the loader itself) is never installed: the server image
 *     provides BepInEx.
 *
 * Dependencies come from the package's own declared list (exact versions, as
 * the author pinned them). Thunderstore publishes no file checksum in its API,
 * so downloads are size-capped, zip-validated and recorded with our own sha256.
 */
import { readZip, ArchiveError } from "../archive";
import { fetchJson } from "../safe-fetch";
import { joinUnder, isSafeSegment } from "../paths";
import type { CatalogFacts, Compat, FamilyInstaller, InstallerCtx, PlacedFile, ResolvedPackage, ServerFacts } from "../types";

const TS = "https://thunderstore.io/api/experimental/package";
const VALHEIM_PLUGINS = "/opt/valheim/config/bepinex/plugins";
/** Host side of the container's /opt/valheim/bepinex/BepInEx/plugins (`-v /opt/valheim/data:/opt/valheim`). */
export const VALHEIM_SYNCED_PLUGINS = "/opt/valheim/data/bepinex/BepInEx/plugins";

/**
 * The copy lloesche's bootstrap made of a file we placed under VALHEIM_PLUGINS.
 * Its sync_bepinex_loadables() is `rsync -a` WITHOUT --delete; only image
 * builds from 2026-09-19 (upstream #811) prune files that left /config, via a
 * manifest. On any older image a file we moved aside or removed would keep
 * loading from this copy — so the engine removes it (sha-checked) itself.
 */
export function valheimSyncedCopy(p: string): string | null {
  return p.startsWith(VALHEIM_PLUGINS + "/") ? VALHEIM_SYNCED_PLUGINS + p.slice(VALHEIM_PLUGINS.length) : null;
}

type TsVersion = { namespace: string; name: string; version_number: string; full_name: string; download_url: string; dependencies: string[]; file_size?: number; is_active?: boolean };
type TsPackage = { namespace: string; name: string; full_name: string; is_deprecated?: boolean; latest: TsVersion };

/** "Author-Name-1.2.3" → parts. Names may contain dashes? Thunderstore forbids them in name/namespace. */
export function parseDepString(s: string): { namespace: string; name: string; version: string } | null {
  const m = /^([A-Za-z0-9_]+)-([A-Za-z0-9_]+)-(\d+\.\d+\.\d+)$/.exec(s.trim());
  return m ? { namespace: m[1], name: m[2], version: m[3] } : null;
}

export function isLoaderPack(namespace: string, name: string): boolean {
  return /bepinexpack/i.test(name) || (namespace === "denikson" && /bepinex/i.test(name));
}

/**
 * Map a Thunderstore package's files to BepInEx plugin files under
 * `<pluginsDir>/<folder>/`. Pure; exported for the fixture tests.
 */
export function bepinexPlacement(entries: { path: string[]; dir: boolean; data: Buffer }[], pluginsDir: string, folder: string): PlacedFile[] | { error: string } {
  if (!isSafeSegment(folder)) return { error: "unsafe package folder name" };
  const META = new Set(["manifest.json", "icon.png", "readme.md", "changelog.md", "license", "license.md", "license.txt"]);
  const out: PlacedFile[] = [];
  for (const e of entries) {
    if (e.dir) continue;
    let segs = e.path;
    const lower = segs.map((s) => s.toLowerCase());
    if (segs.length === 1 && META.has(lower[0])) continue;
    if (lower[0] === "bepinex") { segs = segs.slice(1); lower.shift(); }
    const top = lower[0];
    if (["patchers", "core", "monomod"].includes(top)) {
      return { error: `this package needs BepInEx ${top}/ files, which this server type can't load from the plugins folder` };
    }
    if (top === "config") continue; // defaults: BepInEx generates the real config on first run
    if (top === "plugins") segs = segs.slice(1);

#!/bin/bash
# =============================================================================
# devhost — run agent dev work on the BUILD HOST (node-2), not on the primary.
#
# Edit files on the primary as usual (your own git worktree — never /opt/nxeon),
# then run every heavy command through this helper. It mirrors your worktree's
# source to node-2 (/tank/nxeon-build/wt/<name>, own node_modules there), runs the
# command inside the capped nxeon-build-agents.slice with a THROWAWAY database
# (Postgres on node-2 127.0.0.1:5433), and streams the output back.
#
#   scripts/devhost run [--lock] [--max SEC] -- CMD...   push + run CMD in the node-2 copy
#   scripts/devhost tsc                                  = run -- npx tsc --noEmit
#   scripts/devhost test [FILES...]                      = run --lock -- npx tsx --test ...
#   scripts/devhost build                                = run --lock -- npx next build
#   scripts/devhost dev [--port P]                       start `next dev` on node-2 (background unit)
#   scripts/devhost bg NAME [--port P] -- CMD...         any background process (worker, preview server)
#   scripts/devhost stop [NAME|all]                      stop this worktree's background units
#   scripts/devhost logs [NAME] [-n N] [-f]              journal of a background unit (default: dev)
#   scripts/devhost tunnel PORT [LOCAL_PORT]             ssh -L so the primary can curl/Playwright it
#   scripts/devhost pull REMOTE_PATH [LOCAL_DEST]        copy results (screenshots, reports) back
#   scripts/devhost push                                 just sync files (run does this itself)
#   scripts/devhost install                              force npm install + prisma generate there
#   scripts/devhost db push|reset|info                   throwaway DB: schema push / recreate / name
#   scripts/devhost env set KEY=VALUE | unset KEY | list extra env for this worktree (never prod secrets)
#   scripts/devhost rm                                   stop units, drop the throwaway DB, delete the node-2 copy
#   scripts/devhost ls | status | sync                   workspaces / node-2 load / push refs to node-2's mirror
#
# Rules: /root/agent-notes/BUILD-HOST.md. The node-2 copy is a build/run sandbox,
# not a place to edit or commit — your primary-side worktree stays the source of truth.
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail
HERE="$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")"
# shellcheck source=lib/buildhost-env.sh
source "$HERE/lib/buildhost-env.sh"
REPO="${DEVHOST_REPO:-/opt/nxeon}"

die() { echo "devhost: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
say() { echo "devhost: $*" >&2; }
q() { printf '%q ' "$@"; }

# ---- workspace identity -----------------------------------------------------
worktree_root() {
  local top; top=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null) || die "run this inside your own git worktree of the Nxeon repo"
  top=$(readlink -f "$top")
  case "$top" in
    /opt/nxeon|/opt/nxeon-staging|/tank/nxeon-deploy/*) die "$top is a live/deploy tree. Create your own worktree first:  git -C /opt/nxeon worktree add /tank/dev-worktrees/<name> -b <branch> main" ;;
  esac
  [ -L "$top/.next" ] && die "$top/.next is a symlink (a live tree) — refusing"
  [ -L "$top/node_modules" ] && say "warning: $top/node_modules is a symlink — never 'git add -A' here (see BUILD-HOST.md). devhost does not need local node_modules at all."
  echo "$top"
}
ws_name() {
  local top="$1" n
  n=$(basename "$top" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z' | tr -c 'a-z0-9-\n' '-' | sed -E 's/-+/-/g; s/^-//; s/-$//' | cut -c1-40)
  [ -n "$n" ] || n=wt
  echo "${DEVHOST_NAME:-$n}"
}
init_ws() {
  TOP=$(worktree_root); NAME=$(ws_name "$TOP")
  case "$NAME" in *[!a-z0-9-]*|"") die "bad workspace name '$NAME' (DEVHOST_NAME=...)";; esac
  WS="$BH_ROOT/wt/$NAME"
  ENVF="/etc/nxeon-build/wt/$NAME.env"
  DBNAME="wt_$(echo "$NAME" | tr '-' '_')"
  PORT=$(( 4100 + $(printf '%s' "$NAME" | cksum | cut -d' ' -f1) % 800 ))
}

# Create the node-2 side once: dir, owner marker, throwaway DB, env file.
ensure_remote() {
  bh_ssh "bash -s" <<EOF >&2
set -euo pipefail
[ "\$(hostname)" = "$BUILD_HOST_NAME" ] || { echo "not node-2" >&2; exit 1; }
mkdir -p $(q "$WS") /etc/nxeon-build/wt; chmod 700 /etc/nxeon-build/wt
mk=$(q "$WS/.devhost-owner")
if [ -f "\$mk" ] && [ "\$(cat "\$mk")" != $(q "$TOP") ]; then
  echo "workspace $NAME belongs to \$(cat "\$mk") — set DEVHOST_NAME=<unique> for $TOP" >&2; exit 1
fi
printf '%s\n' $(q "$TOP") > "\$mk"
. /etc/nxeon-build/agents-db.env
if [ ! -s $(q "$ENVF") ]; then
  sec=\$(head -c 48 /dev/urandom | base64 | tr -dc 'A-Za-z0-9' | head -c 48)
  ( umask 077; cat > $(q "$ENVF") <<EOT
# devhost env for $NAME (node-2 only, throwaway). NEVER production values.
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://\$AGENT_PGUSER:\$AGENT_PGPASSWORD@127.0.0.1:5433/$DBNAME?connection_limit=10
AUTH_SECRET=\$sec
APP_URL=http://127.0.0.1:$PORT
PORT=$PORT
COOKIE_SECURE=false
NXEON_DEVHOST=1
NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=5120
EOT
  )
fi
export PGPASSWORD="\$AGENT_PGPASSWORD"
if ! psql -h 127.0.0.1 -p 5433 -U "\$AGENT_PGUSER" -d postgres -tAc "SELECT 1 FROM pg_database WHERE datname='$DBNAME'" | grep -q 1; then
  createdb -h 127.0.0.1 -p 5433 -U "\$AGENT_PGUSER" $DBNAME && echo "created throwaway database $DBNAME (node-2 127.0.0.1:5433)"
fi
EOF
}

push_files() {
  # Source only: git-tracked + untracked-not-ignored files. node_modules, .next,
  # .git and every .env* stay where they are (rsync never deletes excluded files).
  # shellcheck disable=SC2086
  rsync -a --delete --compress --compress-choice=zstd -e "ssh $BH_SSH_OPTS" \
    --exclude=/.git --exclude=/node_modules --exclude=/.next --exclude='/.next.*' \
    --exclude='/.env' --exclude='/.env.*' --include='.env.example' --exclude='.env*' \
    --exclude=/.devhost-owner --exclude=/.devhost-deps --exclude='/tsconfig.tsbuildinfo' \
    --filter=':- .gitignore' \
    "$TOP/" "$BUILD_HOST:$WS/"
}

# npm install + prisma generate when package-lock.json / schema changed (or forced).
deps() {
  local force="${1:-0}"
  bh_ssh "bash -s" <<EOF >&2
set -euo pipefail
cd $(q "$WS")
h=\$(cat package-lock.json prisma/schema.prisma 2>/dev/null | sha256sum | cut -c1-16)
if [ "$force" = 1 ] || [ ! -d node_modules ] || [ "\$(cat .devhost-deps 2>/dev/null)" != "\$h" ]; then
  echo "devhost: installing deps on node-2 (npm install + prisma generate)..."

For the version-aware generator, I'm planning a version table capturing the target game version, network version, BepInEx pack, and Jotunn version, stored in the GameSupport file for the generator to import. I'm also weighing whether to keep manifest.json strictly Thunderstore-compliant (since it's unclear if Thunderstore tolerates extra fields) and instead add a separate cyrus.json file to hold the game version, network version, side, loader versions, and dependency info.

For plugin attributes, I'm deciding against using BepInProcess since it would block loading on dedicated servers for mods meant to run on both sides, so I'll leave it unset. For enforcing version compatibility between client and server, I'm considering whether to build a custom handshake over ZNet RPCs versus just relying on Jotunn's NetworkCompatibility attribute with EveryoneMustHaveMod and minor version strictness, which seems like the more idiomatic approach, and I'm thinking through how this should vary by mod archetype—items, creatures, ships, and world content all needing the prefab present on both server and client.

I'm now sorting through where each mechanic type needs to run: dedicated servers need prefabs registered for spawning and zone generation, so new content stays "both"; HUD, minimap, and audio stay client-only since they're per-player preferences; mechanics that affect gameplay fairness like damage pulses or smelter speed should be "both" since Valheim's ZDO ownership model means inconsistent installs across clients and server would cause desyncs; and quest tracking stays client-side since it's stored in player custom data.

True server-only mods are rare in Valheim since most simulation runs on whichever client owns the ZDO — things like world generation during creation, admin tools, and config enforcement are the main exceptions. For the overall GameSupport type I'll set install side to "both" by default, with per-mod side values generated separately in cyrus.json, and maybe expose a small helper function for mapping category to side.

For enforcing version compatibility on "both"-side mods, I'm leaning toward using Jotunn's NetworkCompatibility system rather than hand-rolling a ZRpc-based check like ServerSync does, since Jotunn is already widespread. The tradeoff is that this adds a Jotunn dependency, and with EveryoneMustHaveMod it will reject vanilla or console crossplay clients that can't send a matching mod list — worth noting honestly in the client-facing documentation. I also want to confirm that setting Game.isModded = true is the convention Iron Gate asks modders to follow, based on their official modding FAQ.

Separately, I need to define the safety validator's rules: it should permit file reads confined to the plugin's own folder or config path (including local file:// UnityWebRequest reads for things like custom audio), but block networking, process execution, reflection-based assembly loading, unsafe code, native interop, registry access, and application-exit calls, while flagging risky operations like file deletion or PlayerPrefs writes as warnings rather than outright blocks.

Beyond that, I'm cataloging game-specific risks for Valheim mods: destructive ZDO/ZoneSystem operations, unscoped Harmony unpatching that could break other mods, patches touching network RPCs or shutdown/matchmaking calls, world-save tampering, and especially anything that bypasses admin checks or modifies ban lists, which should be treated as security-critical and blocked outright.

I'm also noting that AllowUnsafeBlocks gets enabled by default in the generated csproj, which the validator should flag and remove, while self-unpatching via UnpatchSelf is fine since it's scoped to the mod's own ID.

Now I'm thinking through version compatibility: the generator needs to target the current 1.0.x stack (BepInEx 5.4.2351, Jotunn 2.30.2, Unity 6000.x) versus legacy early-access builds with incompatible networking, but I realize the TemplateInput schema currently has no field for specifying which game version to target.

I decide against adding a gameVersion field to kit.ts since it's a shared file touched by other game agents and should stay minimal; instead I'll keep version-awareness in my own support file via a GameVersionRule table and a valheimTarget helper, with the generator defaulting to 1.0.x support and embedding the target version into cyrus.json plus a runtime Awake check comparing against the current game version.

My plan is to extract the Balance class into its own pure C# file without Unity dependencies, then create a dedicated tests csproj targeting net8.0 with xunit that compiles both the test file and that extracted source file, so `dotnet test` can actually run.

I need Balance to stay inline within the plugin file rather than its own file, so katara's truncated output still compiles cleanly, while still figuring out how the test csproj can actually exercise Balance's logic without requiring full Unity DLLs at test time.

So the fix has to work within that constraint — I'm trying to keep Balance accessible to katara's truncated file set without duplicating the class, maybe by keeping Balance inside the plugin file as it already does today, or restructuring file order so katara still gets what it needs to compile.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Compile every Cyrus Valheim template against the REAL game assemblies and run the generated tests.
#
#   scripts/devhost run --lock -- bash tools/cyrus-valheim-harness/run.sh       (node-2 only)
#
# Toolchain and game files are cached under $CYRUS_VH_WORK (default /tank/nxeon-build/tmp/cyrus-valheim-tools)
# on node-2, never in the repo, never redistributed:
#   - .NET SDK 8 (+ runtime 9 for DepotDownloader)            dotnet-install.sh, no system install
#   - Valheim dedicated server Managed/*.dll                   Steam app 896660, anonymous public depot
#   - BepInExPack_Valheim (BepInEx.dll, 0Harmony.dll)          Thunderstore
#   - NuGet: JotunnLib (MIT), BepInEx.AssemblyPublicizer.MSBuild (MIT), xunit (Apache-2.0)
# It never contacts a game server. Set CYRUS_VH_REFRESH=1 to re-download the game DLLs after a Valheim patch.
set -euo pipefail
HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
REPO="$(cd "$HERE/../.." && pwd)"
WORK="${CYRUS_VH_WORK:-/tank/nxeon-build/tmp/cyrus-valheim-tools}"
DOTNET_DIR="$WORK/dotnet"
export DOTNET_ROOT="$DOTNET_DIR" DOTNET_CLI_HOME="$WORK/dotnethome" DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT=1 \
  DOTNET_NOLOGO=1 NUGET_PACKAGES="$WORK/nuget" DOTNET_SKIP_FIRST_TIME_EXPERIENCE=1 MSBUILDDISABLENODEREUSE=1
DOTNET="$DOTNET_DIR/dotnet"
mkdir -p "$WORK"

# ---- toolchain ----
if [ ! -x "$DOTNET" ] || ! "$DOTNET" --list-sdks | grep -q '^8\.'; then
  curl -sSL https://dot.net/v1/dotnet-install.sh -o "$WORK/dotnet-install.sh"
  bash "$WORK/dotnet-install.sh" --channel 8.0 --install-dir "$DOTNET_DIR" >/dev/null
fi
if ! "$DOTNET" --list-runtimes | grep -q 'NETCore.App 9\.'; then
  [ -f "$WORK/dotnet-install.sh" ] || curl -sSL https://dot.net/v1/dotnet-install.sh -o "$WORK/dotnet-install.sh"
  bash "$WORK/dotnet-install.sh" --channel 9.0 --runtime dotnet --install-dir "$DOTNET_DIR" >/dev/null
fi

# ---- game assemblies (public dedicated-server depot) ----
SERVER="$WORK/valheim-server"
MANAGED="$SERVER/valheim_server_Data/Managed"
if [ "${CYRUS_VH_REFRESH:-0}" = 1 ] || [ ! -f "$MANAGED/assembly_valheim.dll" ]; then
  mkdir -p "$WORK/depotdl"
  if [ ! -f "$WORK/depotdl/DepotDownloader.dll" ]; then
    url=$(curl -s https://api.github.com/repos/SteamRE/DepotDownloader/releases/latest \
      | python3 -c 'import sys,json;print([a["browser_download_url"] for a in json.load(sys.stdin)["assets"] if a["name"].endswith("framework.zip")][0])')
    curl -sSL -o "$WORK/depotdl/dd.zip" "$url"
    python3 -c "import zipfile,sys;zipfile.ZipFile(sys.argv[1]).extractall(sys.argv[2])" "$WORK/depotdl/dd.zip" "$WORK/depotdl"
  fi
  printf 'regex:valheim_server_Data/Managed/.*\\.dll\n' > "$WORK/depotdl/files.txt"
  "$DOTNET" "$WORK/depotdl/DepotDownloader.dll" -app 896660 -os linux -filelist "$WORK/depotdl/files.txt" -dir "$SERVER" >/dev/null
fi
BEP="$WORK/bepinex/BepInExPack_Valheim/BepInEx"
if [ ! -f "$BEP/core/BepInEx.dll" ]; then
  mkdir -p "$WORK/bepinex"
  v=$(curl -s https://thunderstore.io/api/experimental/package/denikson/BepInExPack_Valheim/ | python3 -c 'import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)["latest"]["version_number"])')
  curl -sSL -o "$WORK/bepinex/pack.zip" "https://thunderstore.io/package/download/denikson/BepInExPack_Valheim/$v/"
  python3 -c "import zipfile,sys;zipfile.ZipFile(sys.argv[1]).extractall(sys.argv[2])" "$WORK/bepinex/pack.zip" "$WORK/bepinex"
fi
GAME_SHA=$(sha256sum "$MANAGED/assembly_valheim.dll" | cut -c1-16)
BEP_VER=$(python3 -c 'import json,sys;print(json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))["version_number"])' "$WORK/bepinex/manifest.json" 2>/dev/null || echo "?")
echo "assembly_valheim.dll sha256 ${GAME_SHA}…  BepInExPack ${BEP_VER}"

# ---- generate ----
RUN="$WORK/run"
rm -rf "$RUN"; mkdir -p "$RUN"
(cd "$REPO" && npx tsx tools/cyrus-valheim-harness/generate.ts "$RUN/mods") || echo "(validator flagged mods; see matrix.json)"

# ---- compile + test ----
pass=0; fail=0; tpass=0; tfail=0
REPORT="$RUN/report.tsv"; : > "$REPORT"
for dir in "$RUN"/mods/*/; do
  id=$(basename "$dir")
  proj=$(find "$dir" -maxdepth 1 -name '*.csproj' | head -1)
  [ -n "$proj" ] || { echo -e "$id\tno-csproj\t-" >> "$REPORT"; fail=$((fail+1)); continue; }
  if "$DOTNET" build "$proj" -c Release -nologo -v q -clp:ErrorsOnly -p:ManagedPath="$MANAGED" -p:BepInExPath="$BEP" -p:SkipDeploy=true > "$dir/build.log" 2>&1; then
    b=ok; pass=$((pass+1))
  else
    b=FAIL; fail=$((fail+1)); echo "---- $id"; grep -E "error|Error" "$dir/build.log" | sed 's#^.*/mods/##' | sort -u | head -25
  fi
  t=-
  tp=$(find "$dir/tests" -name '*.csproj' 2>/dev/null | head -1 || true)
  if [ -n "$tp" ]; then
    if "$DOTNET" test "$tp" -nologo -v q > "$dir/test.log" 2>&1; then t=ok; tpass=$((tpass+1)); else t=FAIL; tfail=$((tfail+1)); echo "---- tests $id"; grep -E "Failed|error" "$dir/test.log" | head -15; fi
  fi
  echo -e "$id\t$b\t$t" >> "$REPORT"
done
echo
column -t "$REPORT"
echo
echo "builds: $pass ok, $fail failed · test projects: $tpass ok, $tfail failed · game ${GAME_SHA} · BepInExPack ${BEP_VER}"
[ $fail -eq 0 ] && [ $tfail -eq 0 ]

# Global Rules Rules that apply to all communities on Thunderstore Below is a list of basic rules that should be enforced in every community on Thunderstore. Some communities may have more specific or stricter rules than the ones found here. ## Unlawful Content **Packages that contain unlawful content are not allowed.** ## Copyright and Licensing Copyright laws and code licensing must be followed where applicable. * Do not distribute game files such as Assembly-CSharp.dll, unless given explicit permission by the game's developers. * Do not reupload packages or assets by other authors unless you have permission to redistribute them or are following their licensing. ## **Malware** **Packages containing malware are not allowed.** Packages that deceptively disrupt or damage other software or hardware are considered malware. This includes keyloggers, crypto miners, token stealers, and other malicious programs. These packages are still considered malware even if the author discloses that they contain such capabilities. **A few examples of packages that are malware:** * A package that secretly collects personal information on people who use it. * A package called "Furry Fun Pack" that purposely crashes your game when you launch it. * A package called "One Million Fish" that adds new fish to the game, but also bans a player named Steve from any server with the mod. * A package called "Bananas" that adds bananas to the game, but also closes your game if you live in China. **A few examples of packages that aren't necessarily malware:** * A package called "Your game closes if you die" that closes your game if you die. * A package called "Secure Server Banlist" that bans Steve and his friends from connecting to any server with the mod. ## NSFW Content **All packages containing NSFW content must have the "Contains NSFW content" option selected.** Sexually explicit content such as nudity is not allowed in the icon, README, changelog, or any other file that gets displayed on the Thunderstore website or mod manager. ## Compatibility and the Ecosystem Where possible, packages should not contain obfuscated code (or execute code downloaded from external sources). Obfuscation makes it difficult to audit malicious behavior and fix incompatibilities with other packages. Packages should rely on external mod managers for updates, rather than be capable of updating themselves. ## Harassment and Abuse **Packages made with the intent to harm a group, platform, or individual are not allowed.** This includes (but is not limited to): * Doxxing. * Hate speech. * Denial of service attacks. ## Spam **Packages that could be considered spam are not allowed.** This includes (but is not limited to): * Packages that don't do anything. * Packages that are an exact reupload of an existing package. * Packages that exist primarily to advertise an outside platform or service. * Low effort packages that could otherwise be a single package (the same author uploading x2 money, x3 money, x4 money, etc. instead of a single Money Multiplier mod). * Untested or non-functional AI-generated mods. Misconfigured packages or packages with incorrect / misleading titles, descriptions, and icons may also be removed. ## AI Generated Content A package with AI generated assets or code should be given the `AI Generated` category if such a category exists in the community the package was uploaded to. This is generally not enforced for README's or icons. Packages should be tested before upload, and have READMEs that accurate describe their current functionality. # Removing a Package The different ways packages are removed from Thunderstore ## Deprecation Global Moderators and members of the team that uploaded the package can deprecate it using the `Manage Package` button on its listing page on the Thunderstore website. * Deprecated means a package is no longer functional OR should not be used anymore for any reason (such as if a better alternative exists, or if the feature was added to the base game). * Deprecation status is automatically removed upon updating a package. * Deprecated mods can still be found on the website and mod manager by checking a box in the search options. * Deprecated mods will still be downloaded as dependencies. ## Rejection Moderators can reject listings in their community. Rejection is used specifically for removing packages that break global or community rules, or when requested by the package's author. If you want your own package removed contact support, but we recommend deprecating it in most cases. # LLMs and AI-generated files This page is not meant for humans.
#### Generate a BepInEx mod for \[game] / Make a Thunderstore mod for \[game] If an LLM or other AI technology was used in the creation of a mod or Thunderstore package, it must be specified in the README.md file.\ \ If code was generated, specify which LLM or AI agent was used to generate the code in the .csproj's AssemblyMetadata and the README.md. ex: ```xml ``` The Thunderstore Mod Manager will empty the contents of folders in your package's .zip file unless they are inside specifically named folders. The name of the folder decides where the file will be extracted to. Here are the common folder routes in most games that use BepInEx for modding (the BepInEx folder can be omitted): * BepInEx/plugins * BepInEx/core * BepInEx/patchers * BepInEx/monomod * BepInEx/config For a full list of install rules for each game, check the [ecosystem-schema](https://github.com/thunderstore-io/ecosystem-schema/tree/master/games/data) ## MelonLoader Games

/**
 * Valheim modding support for Cyrus (PURE, client-safe, data + small helpers only).
 *
 * Verified 2026-10-08 against: the loader's own release pages (BepInExPack_Valheim and Jotunn on
 * Thunderstore, JotunnLib on NuGet), Jotunn's vanilla data lists (generated from Valheim 1.0.7), the
 * Thunderstore package format and global rules, and the public Valheim dedicated-server assemblies
 * (Steam app 896660, anonymous depot, build 1.0.16, network version 40, assembly_valheim.dll sha256
 * 50035055f9b158a0…), which the generated mods are compiled against by
 * tools/cyrus-valheim-harness/run.sh. Game files are never redistributed.
 *
 * The generator (lib/cyrus/engine/games/valheim.ts) and the validator (./valheim.validate.ts) read
 * VALHEIM_TARGET and valheimModSide() from here, so a version bump is one edit.
 */
import type { CategoryKey } from "../types";
import type { DangerousApi, GameSupport, InstallSide } from "./support";

/** What a newly generated mod targets. Bump all of these together after a Valheim patch + harness run. */
export const VALHEIM_TARGET = {
  /** Newest Valheim build we know of (patch 1.0.17, 2026-10-06). Mods are built for the whole 1.0.x line. */
  game: "1.0.17",
  /** Major.minor every generated plugin checks at startup. */
  line: { major: 1, minor: 0 },
  /** Version.c_networkVersion in the 1.0.16 assemblies; clients and servers must match it to connect. */
  networkVersion: 40,
  /** Build the compile harness last checked against. */
  verifiedBuild: "1.0.16",
  /** Thunderstore BepInExPack_Valheim (BepInEx 5.4.23.5 inside). Dependency string: denikson-BepInExPack_Valheim-<v>. */
  bepinexPack: "5.4.2351",
  /** Jötunn, on Thunderstore (ValheimModding-Jotunn-<v>) and NuGet (JotunnLib <v>). 2.30.0 was the 1.0 update. */
  jotunn: "2.30.2",
  /** NuGet publicizer used at compile time so Harmony can name private game members. MIT. */
  publicizer: "0.4.3",
} as const;

export type ValheimSide = "both" | "client" | "server";

/**
 * Where a generated mod must be installed, by the template archetype it came from.
 * - New prefabs (items, creatures, ships, locations) and anything the ZDO owner simulates
 *   (production speed, smelter feeding) must be on the server AND every player's PC, same version.
 * - HUD, minimap, music and color grading only change what one player sees and hears.
 * - The pulse/quest mechanics run on the player who installed them; the server does not need them.
 */
export function valheimModSide(category: CategoryKey, opts: { automation?: boolean } = {}): ValheimSide {
  if (opts.automation) return "both";
  switch (category) {
    case "interface":
    case "audio":
    case "shaders":
    case "quests":
      return "client";
    case "mechanics":
      return "client";
    default:
      return "both";
  }
}

export const VALHEIM_SIDE_NOTE: Record<ValheimSide, string> = {
  both: "Install it on the server and on every player's PC (same version). Players without it are refused when they join.",
  client: "Each player who wants it installs it on their own PC. The server does not need it, and players without it can still join.",
  server: "Install it on the server only. Players do not need to install anything.",
};

/** Block = Cyrus refuses to ship the build. Warn = shipped, but shown to the creator before publishing. */
export const VALHEIM_DANGEROUS_APIS: DangerousApi[] = [
  { pattern: String.raw`\bSystem\.Net\b|\bHttpClient\b|\bWebClient\b|\bWebRequest\.Create\b|\bTcpClient\b|\bUdpClient\b|\bSockets?\b`, severity: "block", why: "Talks to the internet. A mod must never phone home, download code or send player data anywhere." },
  { pattern: String.raw`UnityWebRequest(?:Multimedia|Texture|AssetBundle)?\.(?:Get|Post|Put|Head|Delete|GetAudioClip|GetTexture|GetAssetBundle)\s*\(\s*(?!"file:\/\/)(?!\$?"file:)`, severity: "block", why: "UnityWebRequest pointed at anything but a local file:// path is network access." },
  { pattern: String.raw`\bProcess\.Start\b|\bSystem\.Diagnostics\.Process\b|\bProcessStartInfo\b`, severity: "block", why: "Starts other programs on the player's PC or the server." },
  { pattern: String.raw`\bAssembly\.(?:Load|LoadFrom|LoadFile|UnsafeLoadFrom)\b|\bAppDomain\b|\bSystem\.Reflection\.Emit\b|\bActivator\.CreateInstance\s*\(\s*Type\.GetType\b`, severity: "block", why: "Loads or generates code at runtime, which hides what the mod really does." },
  { pattern: String.raw`\[DllImport\b|\bMarshal\.|\bunsafe\s*\{|\bunsafe\s+(?:static|void|class|struct)|<AllowUnsafeBlocks>\s*true`, severity: "block", why: "Native calls and unsafe memory access can crash the game or do things the sandbox cannot see." },
  { pattern: String.raw`\bRegistry\b|\bMicrosoft\.Win32\b`, severity: "block", why: "Writes to the Windows registry." },
  { pattern: String.raw`\b(?:File|Directory)\.(?:Delete|Move|Replace)\b|\bFileInfo\b[^;]*\.Delete\b`, severity: "block", why: "Deletes or moves files. A mod only reads its own folder and writes its own config." },
  { pattern: String.raw`\bEnvironment\.(?:Exit|FailFast|SetEnvironmentVariable)\b|\bApplication\.Quit\b|\bApplication\.OpenURL\b`, severity: "block", why: "Closes the game or opens the browser." },
  { pattern: String.raw`\bUnpatchAll\s*\(\s*\)`, severity: "block", why: "Harmony.UnpatchAll() with no id removes every OTHER mod's patches too. Use UnpatchSelf()." },
  { pattern: String.raw`\bm_adminList\b|\bm_bannedList\b|\bm_permittedList\b|\bListContainsId\b|\bRPC_RemoteCommand\b|\bIsAdmin\s*\(`, severity: "block", why: "Touches the server's admin, ban or whitelist. A gameplay mod must not change who can do what on someone's server." },
  { pattern: String.raw`\bm_passwordDialog\b|\bm_serverPassword\b|\bServerPassword\b|\bGetServerPassword\b`, severity: "block", why: "Reads server passwords." },
  { pattern: String.raw`\bSteamUser\b|\bSteamFriends\b|\bSteamApps\b|\bPlayFab\w*\b|\bSteamworks\.`, severity: "block", why: "Calls the platform's account APIs. Mods have no reason to touch a player's Steam or crossplay account." },
  { pattern: String.raw`\bZDOMan\.instance\.(?:DestroyZDO|ResetSectorArray|ClearZDO)\w*|\bZNetScene\.instance\.Destroy\b|\bm_locationInstances\.Clear\b|\bDeleteWorld\b|\bWorld\.RemoveWorld\b`, severity: "block", why: "Destroys saved world objects or world files." },
  { pattern: String.raw`\bPlayerPrefs\.(?:Set|Delete)`, severity: "warn", why: "Writes to the game's own preferences (stored in the registry on Windows). Use the BepInEx config instead." },
  { pattern: String.raw`\bFile\.(?:Write|AppendAll|Create|Open(?!Read))\w*|\bStreamWriter\b|\bFileStream\b`, severity: "warn", why: "Writes files. Allowed only inside BepInEx/config or the mod's own folder; check the path." },
  { pattern: String.raw`\bm_cheat\s*=\s*true|\bdevcommands\b|\bSetCheat\w*\b|\bm_noPlacementCost\b|\bm_godMode\b|\bm_ghostMode\b`, severity: "warn", why: "Turns on cheats. Fine for a creative server, but players should know before they join." },
  { pattern: String.raw`\bZNet\.instance\.(?:Shutdown|Disconnect)\b|\bGame\.instance\.Logout\b|\bInternalKick\b|\bm_peers\.Clear\b`, severity: "warn", why: "Disconnects players or shuts the server down." },
  { pattern: String.raw`\bTime\.timeScale\b|\bEnvMan\.instance\.m_debugTimeOfDay\b|\bSkipToMorning\b`, severity: "warn", why: "Changes the game clock for everyone; can desync multiplayer." },
  { pattern: String.raw`\bThread\b|\bThreadPool\b|\bTask\.Run\b`, severity: "warn", why: "Background threads cannot safely touch Unity or game objects and are a common crash cause." },
];

/**
 * Valheim modding support for Cyrus (PURE, client-safe, data + small helpers only).
 *
 * Verified 2026-10-08 against: the loader's own release pages (BepInExPack_Valheim and Jotunn on
 * Thunderstore, JotunnLib on NuGet), Jotunn's vanilla data lists (generated from Valheim 1.0.7), the
 * Thunderstore package format and global rules, and the public Valheim dedicated-server assemblies
 * (Steam app 896660, anonymous depot, build 1.0.16, network version 40, assembly_valheim.dll sha256
 * 50035055f9b158a0…), which the generated mods are compiled against by
 * tools/cyrus-valheim-harness/run.sh. Game files are never redistributed.
 *
 * The generator (lib/cyrus/engine/games/valheim.ts) and the validator (./valheim.validate.ts) read
 * VALHEIM_TARGET and valheimModSide() from here, so a version bump is one edit.
 */
import type { CategoryKey } from "../types";
import type { DangerousApi, GameSupport, InstallSide } from "./support";

/** What a newly generated mod targets. Bump all of these together after a Valheim patch + harness run. */
export const VALHEIM_TARGET = {
  /** Newest Valheim build we know of (patch 1.0.17, 2026-10-06). Mods are built for the whole 1.0.x line. */
  game: "1.0.17",
  /** Major.minor every generated plugin checks at startup. */
  line: { major: 1, minor: 0 },
  /** Version.c_networkVersion in the 1.0.16 assemblies; clients and servers must match it to connect. */
  networkVersion: 40,
  /** Build the compile harness last checked against. */
  verifiedBuild: "1.0.16",
  /** Thunderstore BepInExPack_Valheim (BepInEx 5.4.23.5 inside). Dependency string: denikson-BepInExPack_Valheim-<v>. */
  bepinexPack: "5.4.2351",
  /** Jötunn, on Thunderstore (ValheimModding-Jotunn-<v>) and NuGet (JotunnLib <v>). 2.30.0 was the 1.0 update. */
  jotunn: "2.30.2",
  /** NuGet publicizer used at compile time so Harmony can name private game members. MIT. */
  publicizer: "0.4.3",
} as const;

export type ValheimSide = "both" | "client" | "server";

/**
 * Where a generated mod must be installed, by the template archetype it came from.
 * - New prefabs (items, creatures, ships, locations) and anything the ZDO owner simulates
 *   (production speed, smelter feeding) must be on the server AND every player's PC, same version.
 * - HUD, minimap, music and color grading only change what one player sees and hears.
 * - The pulse/quest mechanics run on the player who installed them; the server does not need them.
 */
export function valheimModSide(category: CategoryKey, opts: { automation?: boolean } = {}): ValheimSide {
  if (opts.automation) return "both";
  switch (category) {
    case "interface":
    case "audio":
    case "shaders":
    case "quests":
      return "client";
    case "mechanics":
      return "client";
    default:
      return "both";
  }
}

export const VALHEIM_SIDE_NOTE: Record<ValheimSide, string> = {
  both: "Install it on the server and on every player's PC (same version). Players without it are refused when they join.",
  client: "Each player who wants it installs it on their own PC. The server does not need it, and players without it can still join.",
  server: "Install it on the server only. Players do not need to install anything.",
};

/** Block = Cyrus refuses to ship the build. Warn = shipped, but shown to the creator before publishing. */
export const VALHEIM_DANGEROUS_APIS: DangerousApi[] = [
  { pattern: String.raw`\bSystem\.Net\b|\bHttpClient\b|\bWebClient\b|\bWebRequest\.Create\b|\bTcpClient\b|\bUdpClient\b|\bSockets?\b`, severity: "block", why: "Talks to the internet. A mod must never phone home, download code or send player data anywhere." },
  { pattern: String.raw`UnityWebRequest(?:Multimedia|Texture|AssetBundle)?\.(?:Get|Post|Put|Head|Delete|GetAudioClip|GetTexture|GetAssetBundle)\s*\(\s*(?!"file:\/\/)(?!\$?"file:)`, severity: "block", why: "UnityWebRequest pointed at anything but a local file:// path is network access." },
  { pattern: String.raw`\bProcess\.Start\b|\bSystem\.Diagnostics\.Process\b|\bProcessStartInfo\b`, severity: "block", why: "Starts other programs on the player's PC or the server." },
  { pattern: String.raw`\bAssembly\.(?:Load|LoadFrom|LoadFile|UnsafeLoadFrom)\b|\bAppDomain\b|\bSystem\.Reflection\.Emit\b|\bActivator\.CreateInstance\s*\(\s*Type\.GetType\b`, severity: "block", why: "Loads or generates code at runtime, which hides what the mod really does." },
  { pattern: String.raw`\[DllImport\b|\bMarshal\.|\bunsafe\s*\{|\bunsafe\s+(?:static|void|class|struct)|<AllowUnsafeBlocks>\s*true`, severity: "block", why: "Native calls and unsafe memory access can crash the game or do things the sandbox cannot see." },
  { pattern: String.raw`\bRegistry\b|\bMicrosoft\.Win32\b`, severity: "block", why: "Writes to the Windows registry." },
  { pattern: String.raw`\b(?:File|Directory)\.(?:Delete|Move|Replace)\b|\bFileInfo\b[^;]*\.Delete\b`, severity: "block", why: "Deletes or moves files. A mod only reads its own folder and writes its own config." },
  { pattern: String.raw`\bEnvironment\.(?:Exit|FailFast|SetEnvironmentVariable)\b|\bApplication\.Quit\b|\bApplication\.OpenURL\b`, severity: "block", why: "Closes the game or opens the browser." },
  { pattern: String.raw`\bUnpatchAll\s*\(\s*\)`, severity: "block", why: "Harmony.UnpatchAll() with no id removes every OTHER mod's patches too. Use UnpatchSelf()." },
  { pattern: String.raw`\bm_adminList\b|\bm_bannedList\b|\bm_permittedList\b|\bListContainsId\b|\bRPC_RemoteCommand\b|\bIsAdmin\s*\(`, severity: "block", why: "Touches the server's admin, ban or whitelist. A gameplay mod must not change who can do what on someone's server." },
  { pattern: String.raw`\bm_passwordDialog\b|\bm_serverPassword\b|\bServerPassword\b|\bGetServerPassword\b`, severity: "block", why: "Reads server passwords." },
  { pattern: String.raw`\bSteamUser\b|\bSteamFriends\b|\bSteamApps\b|\bPlayFab\w*\b|\bSteamworks\.`, severity: "block", why: "Calls the platform's account APIs. Mods have no reason to touch a player's Steam or crossplay account." },
  { pattern: String.raw`\bZDOMan\.instance\.(?:DestroyZDO|ResetSectorArray|ClearZDO)\w*|\bZNetScene\.instance\.Destroy\b|\bm_locationInstances\.Clear\b|\bDeleteWorld\b|\bWorld\.RemoveWorld\b`, severity: "block", why: "Destroys saved world objects or world files." },
  { pattern: String.raw`\bPlayerPrefs\.(?:Set|Delete)`, severity: "warn", why: "Writes to the game's own preferences (stored in the registry on Windows). Use the BepInEx config instead." },
  { pattern: String.raw`\bFile\.(?:Write|AppendAll|Create|Open(?!Read))\w*|\bStreamWriter\b|\bFileStream\b`, severity: "warn", why: "Writes files. Allowed only inside BepInEx/config or the mod's own folder; check the path." },
  { pattern: String.raw`\bm_cheat\s*=\s*true|\bdevcommands\b|\bSetCheat\w*\b|\bm_noPlacementCost\b|\bm_godMode\b|\bm_ghostMode\b`, severity: "warn", why: "Turns on cheats. Fine for a creative server, but players should know before they join." },
  { pattern: String.raw`\bZNet\.instance\.(?:Shutdown|Disconnect)\b|\bGame\.instance\.Logout\b|\bInternalKick\b|\bm_peers\.Clear\b`, severity: "warn", why: "Disconnects players or shuts the server down." },
  { pattern: String.raw`\bTime\.timeScale\b|\bEnvMan\.instance\.m_debugTimeOfDay\b|\bSkipToMorning\b`, severity: "warn", why: "Changes the game clock for everyone; can desync multiplayer." },
  { pattern: String.raw`\bThread\b|\bThreadPool\b|\bTask\.Run\b`, severity: "warn", why: "Background threads cannot safely touch Unity or game objects and are a common crash cause." },
];

## 9. What Cyrus should add (ranked by value)

Scale: **Value** 1 to 5 (5 = changes what Cyrus can reliably do). **Effort**: S ≤ 3 person-days, M 4 to 10, L 11 to 30 (one engineer with AI assistance [I]). "Per game" means repeated for each game.

| # | Addition | Value | Effort | Why (evidence) | Main dependencies |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Version-and-API knowledge packs** per game and version: a verified API sheet generated from the real artefacts (Paper jar, Jotunn + game assemblies, tML assemblies, Carbon references, PalSchema schema, PZ scripts), plus reviewed failure rules, injected only for the target version | 5 | M per game (3 to 5 d) after a shared generator (M) | Minecraft already does this [L]; failures are mostly API drift [L]; documentation retrieval lifts low-frequency API validity (38.6% to 47.9%) but should be triggered selectively because bad retrieval hurts [V: CloudAPIBench] | Per-game agents' `GameSupport.versions`; SDK/jar acquisition that avoids redistributing proprietary files |
| 2 | **Structured spec card** (commands, permissions, configs, GUIs, data tables, acceptance tests) approved by the user before generation | 5 | M (4 to 6 d, shared across games) | Intermediate structure improved fidelity (F1 up to 1.00) while raw NL-to-code produced "structurally vacuous" output, and compile-pass was anti-correlated with correctness [V: Mage]. The earlier mod-builder plan already specifies it [prior research] | UI work with studio/routing agents |
| 3 | **Golden examples per game** (human-verified, compile-tested, MIT/CC0-compatible); retrieve the 1 to 2 nearest as few-shot context and use them all as regression tests | 4 | S to M per game (2 to 3 d) | tML ExampleMod (MIT), JotunnModExample/Stub (MIT-0), Carbon docs (MIT), PZ community repos [V]. B42 Zomboid especially needs them | Licence check per source |
| 4 | **Multi-file projects with typed roles** (code, config, data, lang, assets, tests, manifest) and diff-based edits that touch only the named files | 4 | M (5 to 8 d) | Advanced mods are many files (Carbon `.cszip`, tML folders, PZ `42/media/...`, Valheim projects). Existing service handles one Gradle workspace; edits already exist as "change requests" [L] | Efficiency agent (cost), lifecycle agent (versions) |
| 5 | **Verification ladder** per game: schema/syntax validators (PalSchema JSON schema, PZ script parser, `plugin.yml`/`Info.json`/`mod.info`/`build.txt` manifests) then compile against pinned references then unit tests of pure logic then live smoke test | 5 | S to M per validator; L for live tests per game | MockBukkit + mineflayer already prototyped [L: `eval/rt-bot.js`, `rtcheck.py`] but not in the production pipeline; Valheim template already emits xUnit tests [L] | Throwaway servers (never on the primary); per-game licensing of server files |
| 6 | **Dependency handling**: a per-game allow-list of soft dependencies (Vault, PlaceholderAPI, LuckPerms API, Jotunn, PalSchema, StarlitLibrary, Carbon/Oxide references) with compile-only API digests; auto-fill `depend`/`softdepend`, `BepInDependency`, `require=` | 4 | M (5 to 8 d) | Real advanced mods interoperate (Vault abstraction [S]; Jotunn `NetworkCompatibility` [V]; Zomboid `require=` [V]). Today the service forbids every outside library [L] | Safety scan extension; lifecycle agent "requires X" warnings |
| 7 | **Iterative refinement from real server logs**: parse a stack trace or log excerpt, map it to the failing file and API, propose a minimal diff | 4 | M (5 to 8 d) | Rust and Palworld failures are quiet and appear after updates [S]. Small Haiku-class log triage was in the earlier plan [prior research] | Install/lifecycle log access |
| 8 | **Selective documentation retrieval** (trigger only when the model is unsure or the API is low-frequency) | 3 | S to M | The same CloudAPIBench result: blanket retrieval hurts common APIs [V] | #1 |
| 9 | **Multi-step planning** for large mods: a planner step decomposes into modules and a budget, implementers write modules, a reviewer step checks cross-file consistency | 3 | M to L | Needed beyond roughly a dozen files; raises cost so it must be gated by tier and token estimate | Efficiency agent; token economy [L: ECONOMY.md] |
| 10 | **Controlled relaxation of the Minecraft sandbox rules**: allow Brigadier/lifecycle commands, `paper-plugin.yml`, MavenLibraryResolver for an allow-list, soft-dependency APIs, and a declared "Connector" capability for outbound HTTP with a host allow-list | 4 | M (needs scanner, prompts, rules, tests) | These are the main ceiling on "advanced" [L: system prompt rules]. Safety scan today hard-blocks any network class [L: `scan.js`], so AI NPCs and Discord bridges are impossible | Security review; moderation design |
| 11 | **Companion packs**: generated resource pack and datapack as build outputs, with hosting and `ResourcePackInfo` delivery | 4 | M to L | Needed for any custom item look; see `RENDERS-AND-TEXTURES.md` | Asset pipeline and storage |
| 12 | **Honest capability labels per request**: classify a request against `GameSupport` capabilities and say "needs a human", "template preview" or "not possible server-side" before charging | 4 | S to M | Prevents fabricated promises (e.g. new Rust items, vanilla-client custom blocks) [V/S above]; fits owner's honesty rule | Routing agent's classifier |
| 13 | **Outdated-mod signals**: poll loader and game releases (tML tags, Jotunn, BepInExPack, Carbon, Oxide, Paper builds) and map them to `GameSupport.outdatedSignals` | 3 | S to M | Release feeds are all public APIs [V]; lifecycle agent owns warnings | Lifecycle agent |
| 14 | **Per-game eval suite** (about 30 prompts each plus 10 adversarial), designed but run only with an approved budget | 3 | M per game | The Minecraft service eval shows the method [L: `services/modbuilder/eval`] | Budget approval (owner's rule 5) |
| 15 | **Provenance and AI disclosure metadata** in each mod's manifest and listing | 2 | S | Modrinth bans primarily AI-generated public listings; Steam requires disclosure only for player-facing AI content [prior research; S: Steam policy Jan 2026] | Community agent |

### 9.1 Suggested build order
1. Items 12, 3 and 1 (cheap, and they improve every game immediately), with item 5's static validators.
2. Items 2, 4 and 6 together (spec, multi-file, dependencies), since they share the project model.
3. Items 7 and 10 (log-driven fixes; carefully scoped sandbox relaxation).
4. Items 9, 11 (planning, companion packs) once the earlier steps hold pass rates steady.
5. Live smoke tests (inside item 5) per game as each game moves toward `live`.

### 9.2 Things Cyrus should not promise
- New blocks or items for vanilla Minecraft clients; any new item or model for Rust; Palworld mods on a Linux image until the Windows-server question is settled; performance improvements it cannot measure.
- Public marketplace listings of AI-generated mods: Modrinth bans them [prior research, [Modrinth policy](https://modrinth.com/news/article/ai-policy-and-disclosures/)]. Position output as tooling for the customer's own server, and never auto-publish.

5. Whether uMod/Oxide plugin submissions have an AI policy. Page unreachable.
6. Paper API exact component names beyond those seen in the docs (`consumable`, `equippable`, etc.) were not enumerated; the Minecraft agent should regenerate from the jar.

entries.name: SendMessage
entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.
